limitations: "In the morning" was taken as 08:00 on 12 November 2026, Sydney time; other morning hours before 11:00 were not tried.
Only Chromium was used; the bug is in date arithmetic, not browser behaviour, and the unit test reproduces it without a browser.
Only steps were minimised; the seeded data and the clock were kept.
next_steps: Fix isDueToday to compare local dates (localDate(now)); the regression test turns green when it is right.
Close or link TASK-14 as a likely duplicate after a person confirms it.

outcome.reason: The as-reported candidate (Sydney, 08:00) matched in every run; the afternoon and UTC variations never did, which fits the report's "right again by the afternoon".

localisation.evidence: isDueToday compares the stored local due date with the UTC date. At 08:00 in Sydney (UTC+11) the UTC date is still the day before. The regression test calls isDueToday directly and fails on exactly this; replacing the line with localDate(now) in a scratch copy made all 5 tests pass.

localisation.code: const shown = filter === "today" ? tasks.filter((t) => isDueToday(t, new Date())) : tasks;
localisation.evidence: The "Due today" button sets filter to "today", and render() filters with isDueToday; this is the path the minimal reproduction exercises.

rating.severity_reason: The "Due today" view, a core function of a task list, silently shows the wrong tasks every morning; a user has no sign it is wrong, so the workaround (reading due dates in All) needs them to know about the bug.
rating.reach_reason: Users in time zones ahead of UTC, before their local UTC midnight (all morning in Sydney).

regression_test.approval: write_regression_test was on for this example run

cases: TASK-11: at 8am in Sydney, a task due today is due today
TASK-11: at 8am in Sydney, a task due yesterday is not due today

regression_test.fix_check: In a scratch copy outside the repo, changing dates.js line 17 to `const today = localDate(now);` made both new tests and the 3 existing ones pass. The fix is not applied here.

limitations: Playwright sends both clicks of a double-click with no pause; a person's two clicks are further apart, which may change the rate.
CPU throttling was not tried because it is Chromium-only and Chromium already matched 3 of 3.
The rate is from 23 Firefox runs on one machine; it will differ elsewhere.
next_steps: Disable the Add button synchronously at the start of addTask, or ignore clicks while an add is in flight.

outcome.reason: The as-reported Firefox candidate matched in 2 of 3 runs; 20 further Firefox runs matched 18 times, so the failure is frequent but not every time, as the report says.

localisation.evidence: addTask disables the Add button only after a random delay of up to 25 ms, and awaits persistLater (40 ms) before adding the task. A second click within that window passes the button.disabled guard on line 25, so both clicks add a task. The runs where only one task appeared fit the delay being short enough.

rating.severity_reason: Adding a task, a core function, creates a duplicate, but the duplicate is visible and the workaround is easy: click Add once.
rating.reach_reason: Any user who double-clicks Add, in every browser tried.

regression_test.reason: The repo's only tests are node:test unit tests with no DOM, and the race is in a click handler. The minimal reproduction spec (run/minimal/TASK-12.minimal.spec.json) re-runs it in a browser; an e2e framework would be needed for a regression test.
